# pull = git stash + git pull + git pop

Make `pull` safe on a dirty working tree: stash local changes, pull with rebase, restore the stash — so that updating a branch does not first require deciding what to do with half-finished work.

<!-- 2026-09-16T05:49Z https://github.com/kamilsk/dotfiles/issues/190#issuecomment-5711687225
Code vs intent: `git-pull` installs `trap '{ git stash pop; }' EXIT` inside a function sourced into the interactive shell. In bash the EXIT trap of a sourced function runs when the *shell* exits, so the stash is popped only when the terminal closes (and a failed rebase leaves the tree stashed with the pop pending). In zsh the semantics differ (function-local EXIT trap), which is probably why the author never saw it. `.github/reviews/20260709T130934Z.md` (finding 9) and `.github/reviews/20260710T095546Z.md` finding 3.
-->
